convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I'm saving a candy bar for when things get better. I haven't told anyone."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."

"Sorghum. Remember the leaf, the stem, the smell — that's the whole of it."
"Wild Amaranth — crush the leaf, smell it, taste the stem. That's how you know it."
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
"Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"Okay, real question: what's the funniest thing you've seen since we got here? I desperately need it."
They laugh — really laugh, the first real one you've heard in days. "Okay. Okay, that's good. I needed that."
"Still on that question."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going. Not that it matters."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Columbus, Ohio. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you still sing."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Never mind. You had something to say?"
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others."
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Katarina grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Jude rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"We went over this," Jude says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"That again?" Jude sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"Take care out there."
"I can't reach this properly. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It keeps getting worse. I can't haul or hunt with it like this — and if it festers, I'm done for. Please, clean it out and bind it tight."
Get to their side of the Haven door and stand next to them — then you can help.
"It's nothing, really. What were you saying?"
"Water Chestnut. Remember the leaf, the stem, the smell — that's the whole of it."
"This one is Huckleberry. Look at the leaf, feel the stem, breathe it in. It'll stick."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I've said all I know. The rest is just guessing."
They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."

"Home's a feeling, not a place. I'm chasing the feeling. Some days I get close."
"I rearranged the bunks again last night. Nobody noticed. That's fine — it felt right for an hour."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lines: d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Leroy Wilson is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d41: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d41: 🕯️ Leroy is dead — and the dead hold no treaties. Every link Haven has shakes.

d41: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead. The bond is young — they're still deciding what Haven is, and grief delays the verdict. They'll test the link — count on it, unless Haven answers first: send grain (1,500 kcal), send a speaker (2 days), or let the silence answer. (Trust -8.)
d41: 🕯️ Leroy Wilson is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d41: What Leroy kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d41: "Leroy's gone." Katarina looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Leroy." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d41: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Wanjiru blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wire Snares (Level 1). A loop of wire on a game trail. Simple, effective, ancient. Check at dawn.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Reading the Land (Level 1). Eat the landscape with your eyes first: green + water + sun means food grows here. Start where those three meet.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: The Forager’s Eye (Level 1). You walk slower and see more. Food was always there; now you notice it.
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d41: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d41: 📖 LEARNED: Field Dressing (Level 1). Break down game fast and clean. Less waste, more meat, usable parts.
d41: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d41: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Leroy Wilson, 41 days. The mantle passes to Wanjiru Kamau.
d41: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Wanjiru Kamau, 30 — a Wild food forager. Her hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Echo Location, Lucky Rock, Trophy Room.
d41: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Stalker of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d41: The village's quarrel was with Leroy — and Leroy is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d41: At the grave, Jude, Colin, Ezequiel and 3 more speak for Wanjiru — "Leroy trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d41: The fire knew Wanjiru before the Codex did — her name already carried weight here.

d65: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.

d65: Emberhold watches to see if Haven holds without its dead — and presses the tribute down to 3,000 kcal/week while the chair is empty. They'll test the link. Count on it. (Trust -8.)

d65: 🕯️ Wanjiru's funeral feast: 1,500 kcal from the pantry, and every shaken fire is fed — Emberhold. The village mourns together, and the links hold because the dead are honored, not because the grief was forgotten. (Trust mended — the -8 bought back with grain.)
d65: 🕯️ Wanjiru Kamau is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d65: What Wanjiru kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d65: "Wanjiru's gone." Katarina looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Wanjiru." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d65: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Colin blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.

d65: 📖 LEARNED: Diplomatic Incident (Level 1). Trust builds 2x faster. You're TOO good though — once per week you can start a diplomatic incident: villagers argue, you pick the winner (+trust with them, -trust with the loser).
d65: 📖 LEARNED: Mediation (Level 1). Let each side talk without interruption. Repeat back what you heard. People de-escalate when heard.
d65: 📖 LEARNED: Reading Tracks (Level 1). Fresh tracks have sharp edges. Old tracks crumble. You can tell how recently something passed.
d65: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d65: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Wanjiru Kamau, 65 days. The mantle passes to Colin Singh.
d65: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Colin Singh, 27 — a rail conductor. Their hands know different work now: Bloodhound, Lucky Rock, Night Eyes, Trophy Room, Green Whisper, Bird Whisperer.
d65: ◈ The System updates its file: the new bearer <redacted> "Stalker of the Apex Predator." It had a word for this one before the Codex came.
d65: The village's quarrel was with Wanjiru — and Wanjiru is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d65: At the grave, Jude, Ezequiel, Eduarda and 4 more speak for Colin — "Wanjiru trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d65: The fire knew Colin before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
